newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares end up, cautiously advancing.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares end up, cautiously advancing.

text.p: Austrian shares ended slightly ahead on Friday as the expiry of June ATX futures passed without serious incident and traders forecast the cautious advance would continue barring bearish developments abroad.
The ATX index of 21 blue-chip shares closed 2.51 points up at 1,302.47, after rebounding off a session low of 1,287.94. Traders said activity on the futures market had set the tone.
June ATX went off the board 1.7 points down at 1,295, a little below market expectations, while July rose 7.1 to 1,308 on brisk turnover of 1,343 contracts.
Overall twelve ATX shares finished higher and nine lower.
Traders saw solid support for the index at 1,290. "But it is more likely to move towards previous highs in the region 1,320-1,330," one said.
A second market participant forecast a period of sideways trading around 1,300. "There is no real pressure on the upside or the downside," he said.
High-grade steelmaker Boehler-Uddeholm was the biggest gainer, rising 22 schillings, or 2.35 percent, to 957 schillings. Dealers also pinpointed demand for brewer BBAG and oil group OMV.
Selling pressure centred on regional utility EVN, which dipped to an intra-day low of 1,637 schillings before recovering to 1,650, 19 schillings down on its previous close, on volume of 68,590.
"There is no guarantee that the sell order in EVN has disappeared," a trader said.
Carton board maker Mayr-Melnhof was the biggest percentage decliner. It slipped nine schillings, or 1.45 percent, to 613. -- Vienna newsroom, +43-1 531 12 254
